description.narrative: Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

The project will generate significant socio-economic benefits by improving the livelihoods, food security, and resilience of coastal communities in Mozambique, Madagascar, and the Comoros. Through ecosystem restoration, sustainable fisheries management, and diversified income opportunities such as aquaculture, seaweed farming, eco-tourism, and mangrove beekeeping, the project will increase household incomes and reduce vulnerability to climate and market shocks. Over 3,000 direct beneficiaries, at least 40% women, will gain new skills, access to climate information, and participation in decision-making. Strengthened regional cooperation and value-chain transparency will enhance market access, attract private investment, and promote equitable benefit-sharing, contributing to inclusive and sustainable blue economy growth across the Mozambique Channel.

To restore and sustainably manage marine fisheries and coastal ecosystems in the Mozambique Channel by 2030 through climate-informed governance, ecosystem rehabilitation, and inclusive livelihood diversification benefiting coastal communities.
